As explained in the text following
Definition <REF_0001>, we may view
preordered sets as categories and systems as functors.
Throughout the proof, we will freely shift between these two points of view.
We prove the first statement by constructing a category
<MATH_0001>, corresponding to a directed set<FOOTNOTEOPEN_0001>In fact,
our construction will produce a directed partially ordered set.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0001>, and a cofinal
functor <MATH_0002>. Then, by
Lemma <REF_0002>, the colimit of a diagram
<MATH_0003> coincides with the
colimit of the diagram <MATH_0004>,
from which the statement follows. The second statement is dual to the
first and may be proved by interpreting a limit in <MATH_0005> as
a colimit in <MATH_0006>. We omit the details.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
A category <MATH_0007> is called <EMPHOPEN_0001>finitely generated<EMPHCLOSE_0001> if
there exists a finite set <MATH_0008> of arrows in <MATH_0009>, such that
each arrow in <MATH_0010> may be obtained by composing
arrows from <MATH_0011>. In particular, this implies that <MATH_0012> has
finitely many objects. We start the proof by reducing to the case
when <MATH_0013> has the property that every finitely generated
subcategory of <MATH_0014> may be extended to a finitely
generated subcategory with a unique final object.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Let <MATH_0015> denote the directed set of finite ordinals, which
we view as a filtered category. It is easy to verify that the
product category <MATH_0016> is also filtered,
and the projection
<MATH_0017>
is cofinal.

<STRUCT_0005><STRUCT_0006>
Now let <MATH_0018> be any finitely generated
subcategory of <MATH_0019>.
By using the axioms of a filtered category and a simple induction
argument on a finite set of generators of <MATH_0020>,
we may construct a cocone <MATH_0021> in <MATH_0022>
for the diagram <MATH_0023>. That is, a morphism
<MATH_0024> for every object <MATH_0025> in <MATH_0026>
such that for each arrow <MATH_0027> in <MATH_0028>
we have <MATH_0029>. We can also choose <MATH_0030> such
that there are no arrows from <MATH_0031> to an object in <MATH_0032>.
This is possible since
we may always post-compose the arrows <MATH_0033> with an arrow
which is the identity on the <MATH_0034>-component and
strictly increasing on the <MATH_0035>-component.
Now let <MATH_0036> denote the category consisting of all
objects and arrows in <MATH_0037>
together with the object <MATH_0038>, the identity
arrow <MATH_0039> and the arrows <MATH_0040>.
Since there are no arrows from <MATH_0041> in <MATH_0042>
to any object of <MATH_0043>, the arrow set in <MATH_0044>
is closed under composition, so <MATH_0045> is indeed
a category. By construction, it is a finitely
generated subcategory of <MATH_0046> which has <MATH_0047> as
unique final object. Since, by Lemma <REF_0003>,
the colimit of any diagram <MATH_0048>
coincides with the colimit of <MATH_0049> , this gives the desired

<STRUCT_0007><STRUCT_0008>
The set of all finitely generated subcategories of <MATH_0050>
with a unique final object is naturally ordered by inclusion.
We take <MATH_0051> to be the category corresponding
to this set. We also have a functor

Given any two finitely generated subcategories of

with a unique final object. This shows that <MATH_0060> is directed.

<STRUCT_0009><STRUCT_0010>
Finally, we verify that <MATH_0061> is cofinal. Since any

<MATH_0067> and maps <MATH_0068>
and <MATH_0069> in
<MATH_0070>, we can take <MATH_0071> to be a finitely

<MATH_0072>, <MATH_0073> and the morphisms <MATH_0074>.
The resulting diagram commutes
